title: Partner Success Standup: Agenda & Facilitation Workbook
body:
Purpose and scope:
This workbook is written for recurring partner success standups that double as a lightweight QBR for customers with mid-sized deployments (2–12 dedicated seats/teams). Goal: run a 30–45 minute connector meeting that surfaces renewal risk, aligns on 60-day priorities, and produces concrete owners + measurement. Use for customers that do not require a full executive QBR but do need regular cadence and renewal tracking.

Meeting formats (pick one):
- Lightning Standup (30 min): 10 min health snapshot, 10 min priority alignment, 10 min risk & actions. Best for tactical customers with low executive involvement.
- Extended Partnership Check (45 min): 10 min exec snapshot (1 slide), 15 min product/usage deep-dive, 10 min renewal signal triage, 10 min action owners & deadlines. Best when renewal < 90 days or rollout has open technical blockers.

Attendees (recommended):
- Customer: Primary CSM contact, Engineering/Platform lead (if platform integration), Product sponsor (optional), Procurement/Legal (if renewal nearing).
- Redwood: Assigned CSM (facilitator), Solutions Engineer or AM (tech owner), Renewal Success rep (if renewal < 90 days), Customer Support lead (only for escalations).

Pre-meeting checklist for facilitator (send 3–5 business days prior):
- Confirm attendees and meeting length; escalate to exec brief if more than one exec attending.
- Compile one-page executive snapshot (see template below) and attach as pre-read.
- Run renewal signals audit (see rubric) and flag >1 medium/high signals to the solutions engineer.
- Capture any open GitHub/Support tickets that touch the customer experience in the last 30 days.
- Draft expected outcomes and desired decisions (e.g., sign SOW amendment, freeze rollout date, approve engineering work).

One-page executive snapshot (deliverable - 1 slide):
- Header: Customer name, CSM, date, next renewal date, ARR bucket.
- Top-line: Health score (0–100) and trend (▲/▼/—) with one-sentence rationale.
- Usage highlights: 3 bullets (active users, avg latency, top feature usage).
- Support & reliability: # SEV1/2 incidents last quarter, MTTR trend.
- Risks (3): clear concise risk statements with impact estimate and suggested mitigation.
- Ask / decision needed: single-line call to action (sign, approve, extend trial, commit to pilot).

Facilitation script (compact, for facilitator to read verbatim if needed):
- 0:00–0:03 — Welcome + purpose: "Thanks everyone for joining. Today’s goal is to align on the next 60 days of work, confirm renewal signals, and leave with owners and dates. We’ll start with a 1-slide health check, then dig into usage, blockers, and finish with actions."
- 0:03–0:08 — Exec snapshot review: read top-line health score and 1–2 supporting bullets. Pause for any immediate clarifying questions.
- 0:08–0:18 — Usage & outcomes: "Can you share where the product is delivering value? Any unexpected blockers or shifts in priorities?" Capture 1–2 success stories and 1–2 problems.
- 0:18–0:28 — Risk & renewal signals triage: Present pre-compiled signals; ask customer to validate and rank them. If high risk, propose a mitigation owner.
- 0:28–0:30/0:45 — Actions & close: Confirm owners, deadlines, and next sync. Restate the primary decision ask.

Rapid-risk rubric (use to convert notes into renewal probability):
- High risk (Renewal probability: 0–40%): Multiple blockers (integration, legal, exec disengaged), >1 high-priority bugs blocking production, or >2 SEV incidents in last 60 days.
- Medium risk (Renewal probability: 40–70%): Some adoption gap, mixed executive support, or one outstanding high-priority item with an owner but unclear ETA.
- Low risk (Renewal probability: 70–95%): Healthy usage growth, regular stakeholder cadence, no unresolved high-priority issues.

Signals to check (quick checklist):
- Exec engagement (Y/N and date of last exec contact).
- Contract health (time to renew, upcoming legal reviews).
- Product adoption (active seats, daily/week active users, percent of power users).
- Reliability & incidents (SEV counts, open RT tickets).
- Financial signals (budget cycles, pricing pushback).
- Competitive movement (RFP, POC with another vendor).

Triage playbook for elevated risk: (if risk -> Medium/High)
- Immediately schedule a risk deep-dive (30–60 min) with product/SE/AM.
- Assign mitigation owner and 2-week cadence for status updates.
- Prepare a customer-facing mitigation plan (1 page) summarizing actions, owners, and timelines.
- If legal/procurement is a blocker, loop in Renewal Success and Sales Ops and escalate via CS lead.

Action item template (to paste into meeting notes):
- Action: <short action statement> | Owner: <name> | Due: <YYYY-MM-DD> | Success metric: <how we'll measure completion> | Follow-up meeting: <date or cadence>

Sample invite & pre-read note (email snippet):
"Subject: Partnership Standup — <Customer> — <Date>
Hi all,
Please join our 30-min partnership standup on <date/time>. Attached is a 1-page health snapshot and the list of proposed outcomes. Please review the snapshot beforehand and bring any updates on usage/blocks. If this should be an executive brief instead, let me know.
Thanks,
<CSM name>"

Common objections and suggested responses (short):
- "We don’t have bandwidth for another meeting." — Offer the 30-min Lightning Standup and propose rotating technical deep-dives only when needed.
- "We’re not ready to commit to the renewal." — Surface specific blockers; propose a 30-day remediation plan and a follow-up executive check in.
- "Price concerns." — Capture financial signals, escalate to Sales Ops, and propose structured discounting only with explicit ROI plan and timeline.

Metrics to record in CRM after meeting (minimum fields):
- Health score (numeric)
- Renewal probability (High/Medium/Low)
- Top 3 risks (short bullets)
- Next steps (1–3 actions with owners/dates)
- Executive contact status (last touch date)

Notes on localization of the playbook:
- For enterprise customers, expand the partnership check to 60–90 minutes and include Legal/Procurement and a dedicated Solutions Engineering demo slot.
- For self-serve or low-touch customers, convert this into an async checklist + recorded 15-min video update and capture the same fields in CRM.

Appendix: quick renewal tracking snippet (paste into a tracker sheet):
| customer | next_renewal | renewal_prob | last_exec_touch | top_risk_short | action_owner | action_due |
| <Customer> | <YYYY-MM-DD> | Low/Med/High | <YYYY-MM-DD> | <short> | <name> | <YYYY-MM-DD> |

Open questions / things to iterate on (working notes):
- Should we standardize a single health scoring algorithm across CS? (notes: proposed mix of usage, incidents, exec touch, NPS)
- Can we automate pre-read snapshot generation from product analytics to reduce manual prep time? (owner: product-analytics)
- Potential experiment: split standups into two alternating cadences (exec + tech one week, adoption deep-dive next).

Version history (notes):
- 2025-11-08 initial draft (Lena)
- 2025-12-02 added rapid-risk rubric (Benji)
- 2026-02-10 updated sample invite and expanded triage playbook (Maya)

End of workbook.
